carries: PHOTOS. A run of 104 photos stopped for one prompt: the convention checker found the framing by keyword and matched 'angle' inside 'flatbread tri-ANGLE-s' — the dish's own name — then reported it as a framing with no distance. The framing is the fourth part of every prompt by construction; the checker reads it there, on word boundaries
a prompt outside the convention now sets its own recipe aside, by name, and the rest are photographed; one drifted prompt no longer stops the run

PHOTOS.command read only .env and GENERER.command only cle-api.txt, so a secret placed in one was reported missing by the other — with a message naming the wrong file. Both commands read both files, tolerate spaces around '=', and the message names the variable, not a file

the free list is fourteen meals and fourteen snacks, as publishing.json's own note asked for and no one applied: seven free meals over a fourteen-day window brought every dish back exactly seven days later, which is why last week read as a copy of this one. A test holds the count
under the week, for a parent without a subscription: the first rows of last week, real recipes fading towards the offer card, not tappable — the eye reads there is more instead of meeting a wall

three free recipes still have no photo (sweet-potato-and-chicken-puree, pasta-in-rose-sauce-with-chicken, baked-fish-nuggets); they are hand-rewritten to the standard and stay free. PHOTOS.command takes them, along with the other sixty

the key files were SOURCED, which executes them: a UTF-8 BOM — three invisible bytes TextEdit adds — made the first line a failing command and aborted the file, so a key sitting right there read as missing. Worse, build 195 made PHOTOS.command read cle-api.txt BEFORE .env, so a BOM there hid the key that had always worked. tools/read-keys.py parses both files as data, decoded with utf-8-sig; a value already set is never overwritten. Six shapes tested — BOM, CRLF, export, spaces, quotes, plain — and the split case that broke the run

the pre-flight counted only data/recipes.json and announced '3 images on 25 recipes' while the cycle made 56 of 149 — the imported and generated ones were invisible to it. It reads the whole corpus, and a test pins its count to the cycle's
